notice: Public bibliographic records verified against PubMed. No generated claims, reviewer labels, researcher sessions, or scientific-quality results are included.
topic: How do urban tree canopy effects on heat vary by measurement outcome, spatial scale, time of day, and climate context?

records.title: Street trees provide an opportunity to mitigate urban heat and reduce risk of high heat exposure
records.design_scope: Observational field measurements of summer sidewalk air temperature and street-tree canopy in a Tacoma, Washington neighborhood; verify exact sampling and model details in the article before coding claims.

records.title: The role of urban trees in reducing land surface temperatures in European cities
records.design_scope: Remote-sensing land-surface-temperature and land-cover analysis across 293 European cities; distinguish modeled/observed surface temperature contrasts from pedestrian-level air temperature.

records.title: Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat during summer
records.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
records.design_scope: Bicycle-mounted urban air-temperature sampling across ten Madison, Wisconsin transects with land-cover measures at multiple spatial scales; inspect the paper for sampling and model limitations.

cases.task: Search the topic, open candidate records, and select relevant publications for a project.
review_checks: Each selected record resolves to its PubMed/PMC record
Title, authors, year, DOI and PMID match the record
Unavailable providers and metadata-only access are disclosed

cases.task: Create one row per selected publication and record study setting/design, temperature outcome, spatial scale, time conditions, and stated limitations.
review_checks: Air temperature is distinguished from land surface temperature
Study observations are separated from author interpretation
Every factual row has a source link and the researcher can annotate it

cases.task: Draft a comparative synthesis of what the three records measure and where their results may not be directly comparable.
review_checks: No pooled effect is invented from incompatible outcomes
The synthesis preserves scale, city and time-of-day boundaries
Each claim is separately rated for citation identity and semantic support

cases.task: Draft a proposed study of neighborhood tree canopy and summer heat exposure, explicitly labeling unanswered questions and assumptions.
review_checks: Proposed aims are not presented as observed findings
The rationale links to selected records
Uncertainty and population/geography limits remain visible

cases.task: Propose a field-sampling plan that could compare canopy and impervious-surface conditions while recording relevant weather and spatial context.
review_checks: Methods are labeled proposed until carried out
Each methodological claim has traceable support or is labeled as a design choice
No results or ethics approval are fabricated

cases.task: Draft milestones for protocol design, site selection, measurement, analysis, and researcher review.
review_checks: Generation alone does not alter the project workplan
Only researcher-selected tasks enter a draft after explicit approval
A separate workplan save is required and visible

cases.task: Edit a researcher annotation, save, reload, export the artifact, and compare it with the saved project state.
review_checks: Researcher-authored text survives regeneration and reload
Stale-version conflict preserves both the winner and recoverable local edits
Export retains source identifiers and distinguishes AI draft from approved content

rating_protocol.identity_and_traceability: Record separately whether the citation identifier resolves and bibliographic metadata matches the selected record.
rating_protocol.semantic_support: Two domain researchers independently assess each factual or interpretive claim against the cited source text available to the study.
rating_protocol.prohibition: Source-ID resolution is not evidence that a source supports a scientific claim. The fixture contains no reviewer judgments.
